platform: Omarchy 4.5.0-3, Hyprland 0.56.2, kernel 7.2.15-1-omarchy, x86_64, Quickshell 0.3.2, Node v26.13.0
scope: Live desktop acceptance of the 0.4.6 candidate: the Settings page's two free-text values — the custom refresh or notification number, and the store country code — are no longer Qt text inputs. They are drawn from key events in EntryField.qml, with the editing logic in EntryEdit.js. The clipboard is read only on an explicit paste, out of process, under a two-second timeout and a 4096-byte cap that refuses an oversized read rather than truncating it, so no Qt editable input can stall the shared shell on a clipboard read. The country field takes exactly two letters (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2), upper-cased as they are typed. A field keeps the keyboard when it loses the focus, so the clipboard picker (SUPER+CTRL+V) pastes into it again. The store notifications, the panel, the IPC actions and the install/update/removal lifecycle are unchanged and were re-checked.
install: The development symlink was unlinked (the repository untouched) and the plugin installed from https://github.com/salmun-nister/omarchy-loot-drops with `omarchy plugin add ... --enable --yes`, which cloned cb082f5 (VERSION 0.4.6). The clone was checked out at v0.3.1 to stand in for the previous release, and the user's bar-slot entry was restored with both Epic mobile toggles, Amazon Luna, hideSeen and the country value, with epicNotify temporarily set false so the 0.3.1 baseline rewrite could not fire a burst during the update. The shell was restarted and `omarchy plugin update ... --yes` fast-forwarded the clone to cb082f5; the bar-slot entry kept every value, including amazonEnabled, hideSeen, epicMobileAndroid, epicMobileIos, country and refreshMinutes. Each fetch rewrites seen.json ids, so the pre-lifecycle state file was restored from a backup after the lifecycle; install, update and removal themselves left it in place. Removal deleted the clone, unloaded the widget and removed its entries while seen.json stayed. The development symlink was re-linked, the plugins were rescanned, the plugin was enabled on the right, the original shell.json and seen.json were restored byte-identically (sha256 166689b67848638039e9670674ab450783bb1a3ad3e8121e8f8bd5f6bb1bd395 and 3807bb74fea9a36ced0388d01019743d5b188767fbc5d8e79ace9565dbf34a1c) and the shell was restarted; the plugin loaded and the three Epic ids were back in the baseline.
commands: ln -s /home/kevin/Projects/Omarchy-Loot-Drops ~/.config/omarchy/plugins/salmun-nister.loot-drops; omarchy-shell shell rescanPlugins; omarchy plugin enable salmun-nister.loot-drops right
restore the original shell.json and seen.json; omarchy restart shell

results.detail: ./tests/run passed 82 tests, the real Qt qmllint pass and the helper checks, both from the repository and from the installed clone. omarchy plugin validate . exited 0. validate_plugin.py reports valid with no errors or warnings and an advisory review-required security section with no findings. release_preflight.py reports the release SHA and advisory matches only — collected input, process execution, privilege wording, installer and package-manager surfaces — with no error other than the dirty tree this record itself was. These are limited scans, not a security audit.

results.check: Settings page with the self-drawn fields
results.detail: The live Settings page was captured on this desktop from the installed 0.4.6 clone and shows the country field at the same width as the dropdowns above it, with the two-letter hint, alongside the refresh interval and notification limit controls. The harness reports 13 rows with headers for Epic and Amazon and no QML errors. The panel opened on demand and the settings page rendered on the merged commit.

results.check: Typing, the country rule and the clipboard paste
results.detail: The owner drove the live panel on this tree before the commit was created (the commit contains exactly that tree): clicking the country field selects its value, letters are upper-cased and stop at two, a digit is ignored, Ctrl+V pastes, and SUPER+CTRL+V from the clipboard history pastes into the field, which previously did nothing. The agent cannot click the live panel, so the paste path was also exercised mechanically in a throwaway Quickshell scene (not part of the repository): a real EntryField behind a layer surface that takes the keyboard like the clipboard picker does, then the real /usr/share/omarchy/bin/omarchy-clipboard-paste-text --shift-insert. The field kept the focus item across the deactivation and the pasted value landed. The same scene with the previous behaviour — the field handing the keyboard back to a stand-in key catcher on any end of edit — left the field empty, so the check does detect the defect it guards.

The only clipboard read is the paste process: lib/capped-run as argv, with no shell, under timeout -k 1 2 and a 4096-byte cap that refuses an oversized read instead of truncating it, plus a four-second watchdog. Copying writes Quickshell.clipboardText and never reads. tests/qml-surface.test.mjs fails if runtime QML reintroduces a TextField, TextInput, TextEdit or TextArea, or reaches the clipboard outside that one path; the check ran green in both the repository and the installed clone.

results.check: IPC actions on the live shell
results.detail: `markSeen amazon test-id-046` exited 0 and the id was written to the Amazon acknowledged set in seen.json. `openGame notastore x` and `openGame steam 'bad id'` both exited 0 without opening anything, confirming the validation path. seen.json was restored byte-identically after the test.

./tests/harness/run against the live stores reported 13 rows with headers for Epic and Amazon only (Steam and GOG were empty, so they correctly had no section), laid-out content and no QML errors. This is the transport and layout check, not a substitute for a desktop pass.

results.check: Fresh install, update from 0.3.1 and removal
results.detail: Installed from the repository URL at cb082f5 and enabled, then checked out at v0.3.1 with the user's entry restored and `omarchy plugin update ... --yes` fast-forwarding to cb082f5. The bar-slot entry kept amazonEnabled=true, hideSeen=true, both Epic mobile toggles, country and refreshMinutes=90. `omarchy plugin remove ... --yes` deleted the clone and unloaded the widget; seen.json was left in place. The development symlink, the original shell.json and the pre-lifecycle seen.json were restored and verified by checksum afterwards.
The Settings page capture supplied by the owner was cropped to the panel, 430x614, and staged outside the repository for the release notes. It shows the 0.4.6 country field with its two-letter hint.

limitations: The agent cannot click the live panel, so the typing, the two-letter rule and both paste routes were driven by the owner on the same tree the commit was made from, and the paste path was additionally exercised mechanically in a throwaway scene that is not part of the repository. No bundled or single-game notification was observed live in this run; that path is unchanged and covered by the model tests. Live store contents vary, and GOG's success path remains fixture-only because no giveaway was live. A bar-slot entry pre-seeded with the Epic mobile keys before upgrading from 0.3.1 can announce the current mobile games once, because 0.3.1 never recorded those ids; no released version shipped those keys, so a normal upgrade has them off, and epicNotify was muted for the lifecycle here. The clipboard boundary is checked by a static test and a mechanical scene, not by an audit of a hostile clipboard client. No security audit is claimed; the validators are limited scans.
